name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks. This catches real-world issues without slowing teams down, proving its value before full rollout. The trade-off is temporary noise in logs and extra storage, but it’s the fastest way to gather unbiased data on false positives and edge cases. If the lead approves, we’ll have hard numbers to justify scaling it up.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode trains reviewers to dismiss *all* autofeedback as noise, not just the false positives. A better test is controlled rollout to a single team first—measure impact on review time and signal-to-noise ratio before expanding. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot on one team and comparing reviewer response rates to PR-Agent feedback against a baseline.

name: Overhaul
text: Run the pilot on a team already using PR-Agent’s light-risk flagging—no extra setup needed, cuts the test’s cost to zero. If the signal-to-noise improves, expand to other teams; if not, drop the idea without wasted effort.
